sofia: Heads up — found a perf regression in the AWQ INT8 weight-only path on staging. Group_size=64 workloads with hot KV cache reuse show p95/p99 tail increases (~20-30%) even though p50 is unchanged. Repro steps below, attaching perf flame and kernel chooser trace.

raj: thanks — noticed similar in canary earlier today, thought it was noise. do you have a flamegraph?

sofia: Yup. Flame attached (see below). Main signal is this kernel/pack hotspot during KV unpack when batch contains mixed cached + uncached requests. It seems the kernel chooser falls back to serial-pack path more often.

ming: pinging kernel-chooser owners @raj @jordan. Can you paste the trace output?

sofia: Here are quick repro commands we ran on staging:
```bash
# synthetic workload: 70% cache-hit, group_size=64
PYTHONPATH=. python infra/bench/multi_session.py --model redwood/7b-awq-int8 --group-size 64 --sessions 40 --cache-hit-rate 0.7 --qps 120
```
And a minimal perf record:
```bash
perf record -F 200 -a -g -- sleep 30
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```

sofia: Flame main area: pack/serial_pack -> kv_unpack -> kernel_serial_gemm. Heatmap shows pack overhead per-request increases nonlinearly once mix has >25% cached.

raj: I suspect the issue is the batching heuristic that tries to keep group packing alignment. When some requests are served from KV cache we reduce the amortized cost of packing, but the runtime currently reserializes buffers for the whole batch if even one request needs unpack -> that's expensive.

jordan: Interesting. Does this repro with GPTQ models as well or only AWQ?

sofia: We've only tested on AWQ int8 weight-only so far. Quick check on GPTQ-int8 (same group_size) showed smaller effect (~5-7%), so AWQ-specific kernel path likely different.

ming: Can you share the kernel selection logs? Use TRACE=kernel-chooser to get chooser decisions.

sofia: Pasted chooser snippet:
```text
[chooser] batch_id=842 chooser: preferred=parallel_pack(kernel_v2) fallback=serial_pack(kernel_v1) reason=kv_mismatch
[chooser] batch_id=843 chooser: preferred=parallel_pack(kernel_v2) fallback=serial_pack(kernel_v1) reason=kv_mismatch
[chooser] batch_id=844 chooser: preferred=parallel_pack(kernel_v2) fallback=serial_pack(kernel_v1) reason=group_stride_misaligned
```
This pattern repeats; the fallback path triggers extra memcopies/unpack.

raj: That "kv_mismatch" flag is new — it's emitted when requests in the batch have mixed kv cache state. Looks like the fallback threshold is too aggressive for group_size=64. We tuned conservatively to avoid correctness bugs, but cost is high.

sofia: Agreed. Quick numbers from staging A/B this morning:
- baseline (group_size=32, old heuristic): p99=172ms
- new heuristic + group_size=64: p99=220ms (+28%)
- force-parallel-pack (experimental): p99=178ms (+3%) but saw a couple of rare correctness asserts in 1/10k requests

jordan: Rare correctness asserts are probably tolerable for staging but not prod. We need to identify what edge-case triggers them if we force the parallel pack. Could be alignment/quant-block boundary assumptions for AWQ.

ming: Suggestion: add a fast-path to skip reserialization when a subset of requests has cached KV and the cached payload format matches current pack alignment. Less conservative checks first, then fallback. That reduces memcopy cost without risking correctness.

sofia: Agreed. I prototyped a check that compares request.kv_format_id and batch.pack_alignment. If they match, we avoid full re-pack. Microbench on local reduced pack overhead by ~40% for mixed batches.

raj: Nice. Can you open an RFC PR outlining the check and the required invariants? We'll also want an opt-in runtime flag so we can enable on canaries.

sofia: Will do. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/472 (WIP) — includes test vectors for cached vs uncached mix and a stress job to catch asserts.

perf-bot: perf regression alert detected on staging: run id=stg-2026-03-18-23, delta_p99=+27%. Linked thread: <channel>/2145001234

sofia: Adding telemetry: need heatmap of pack time vs cache-hit fraction for group sizes [16,32,64,128]. If we can show safe operating envelope we can set routing policy knob (prefer smaller group_size when cache-hit rate > X).

jordan: Also check batching heuristics: maybe it's beneficial to split batches by cache-state during scheduling rather than post-facto. That would avoid mixed-batch fallbacks entirely at scheduler level. Tradeoff: smaller effective batch size for cached requests.

raj: I'll prototype scheduler split + opt-in rollout. If scheduler splits, runtime doesn't need heuristics and kernels can assume uniform cache state.

sofia: TL;DR action items:
- sofia: PR with fast-path avoidance of reserialization + tests (WIP)
- raj: prototype scheduler-split and compare throughput/latency tradeoffs
- ming: add kernel-chooser telemetry + flame correlation for canary runs
- jordan: audit AWQ kernel assumptions for parallel-pack correctness edgecases

sofia: I'll run expanded canary tomorrow with the opt-in flag and post numbers. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks — label this high-priority for next sprint planning.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued for staging: runtime:v1.3.8-canary-serializer-fix (triggered by sofia).

sofia: closing loop — initial canary with opt-in fast-path reduced p99 back to ~180ms and CPU utilization down ~8%. Still validating correctness under stress. Will update thread with final sign-off. :white_check_mark:
